questions.q: Which feature is strongly associated with mature Harappan cities?
questions.e: Harappan settlements such as Mohenjo-daro show planned streets, organised blocks and sophisticated drainage. These features indicate urban planning and civic organisation. Iron technology, Buddhist caves and Nagara temples belong to later historical contexts. Remember: town planning and drainage are hallmark Harappan features.

questions.q: Who was Governor-General of India when the Revolt of 1857 began?
questions.e: Lord Canning was Governor-General when the uprising began. After the Government of India Act 1858 transferred authority from the East India Company to the British Crown, he became the first Viceroy. Dalhousie preceded him. Remember: Canning — Revolt of 1857 and transition to Crown rule.

questions.q: Which of these Indian states is crossed by the Tropic of Cancer?
questions.e: The Tropic of Cancer lies at approximately 23½° north latitude. It crosses eight Indian states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram. Meghalaya, Kerala and Punjab are not crossed by it. Remember the eight-state sequence for map-based questions.

questions.q: The Equator is located at which latitude?
questions.e: The Equator is the imaginary great circle at 0° latitude and divides Earth into the Northern and Southern Hemispheres. The Prime Meridian is 0° longitude. The Tropic of Cancer is about 23½° north and the Arctic Circle about 66½° north.

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution abolishes untouchability?
questions.e: Article 17 abolishes untouchability and forbids its practice in any form. Article 14 concerns equality before law; Article 19 protects specified freedoms; Article 21 protects life and personal liberty. Remember: Article 17 — abolition of untouchability.

questions.q: The Directive Principles of State Policy are contained in which Part of the Constitution?
questions.e: Directive Principles are in Part IV, Articles 36–51. They guide the State in making laws and policies for social and economic welfare. Under Article 37 they are not directly enforceable by courts, though they are fundamental to governance. Part III contains Fundamental Rights; Part IVA contains Fundamental Duties.

questions.q: Which institution is responsible for monetary policy in India?
questions.e: The Reserve Bank of India is India's central bank. The Monetary Policy Committee, under the RBI Act framework, determines the policy rate to achieve the inflation target while keeping growth in mind. NITI Aayog is a policy think tank; the Finance Commission recommends fiscal devolution; the CAG audits public accounts.

questions.q: GST in India is primarily a tax on which of the following?
o: Supply of goods or services or both
questions.e: Under the CGST Act, 2017, GST is levied on intra-State supplies of goods or services or both, subject to the statutory framework. Inter-State supplies are generally covered by the IGST framework. Income tax and corporate tax are direct taxes on income or profits. Remember: GST is an indirect tax on supply; technical questions must be checked against current law.

questions.q: The Convention on Biological Diversity was opened for signature at which 1992 event?
questions.e: The Convention on Biological Diversity was opened for signature at the 1992 UN Conference on Environment and Development in Rio de Janeiro. Its three objectives are conservation of biological diversity, sustainable use of its components, and fair and equitable sharing of benefits from genetic resources. Kyoto 1997 is associated with the Kyoto Protocol; Paris 2015 with the Paris Agreement.

questions.q: The ozone layer that absorbs much of the Sun's harmful ultraviolet radiation is mainly found in which layer?
questions.e: Most atmospheric ozone is concentrated in the stratosphere, roughly 10–50 km above Earth's surface. It absorbs much of the Sun's harmful ultraviolet-B radiation. The troposphere is the lowest layer where most weather occurs; ground-level ozone is an air pollutant. Remember: protective ozone layer — stratosphere.

questions.q: What is the SI base unit of electric current?
questions.e: The ampere (A) is the SI base unit of electric current. Volt measures electric potential difference, ohm measures resistance, and watt measures power. Memory aid: current—ampere; voltage—volt; resistance—ohm; power—watt.

questions.q: Which part of the human brain primarily coordinates balance and voluntary movements?
questions.e: The cerebellum coordinates voluntary movement, posture and balance. The cerebrum supports higher functions such as thinking, memory and conscious movement. The medulla oblongata regulates vital involuntary functions such as breathing and heart rate. The hypothalamus helps regulate temperature, hunger, thirst and endocrine functions.

questions.q: Which classical dance-drama tradition is associated with Kerala?
questions.e: Kathakali is a classical dance-drama tradition of Kerala, known for elaborate costumes, facial expressions, hand gestures and stylised storytelling. Bharatanatyam is associated with Tamil Nadu, Kathak developed in North India, and Odissi is associated with Odisha. Mohiniyattam is another classical dance tradition of Kerala.

questions.q: Which component executes program instructions and is commonly called the brain of a computer?
questions.e: The Central Processing Unit (CPU) executes program instructions and performs arithmetic and logical operations. A monitor is an output device, a keyboard is an input device, and a printer produces hard-copy output. The CPU is not the same as long-term storage.

questions.q: Which principal UN organ has primary responsibility for maintaining international peace and security?
questions.e: The UN Security Council has primary responsibility under the UN Charter for maintaining international peace and security. The General Assembly is the main deliberative organ; ECOSOC coordinates economic and social work; the International Court of Justice is the UN's principal judicial organ.

questions.q: Who wrote the novel The Guide?
questions.e: The Guide is a novel by R. K. Narayan, first published in 1958. It follows Raju, a tourist guide whose life changes through his relationship with a dancer and later his unexpected spiritual reputation. Mulk Raj Anand wrote Untouchable; Raja Rao wrote Kanthapura. Remember: The Guide — R. K. Narayan.
